text:
maya: FYI escalated ticket from Acme — Go client streaming gets cut off mid-response. They see partial outputs, occasional duplicate tokens after reconnect, and HTTP 499s. Customer says repro with go-sdk v1.4.0. Need triage asap.

john: Can you drop the minimal repro + client logs + the service request_id?

maya: request_id=req_0b4f8c. Customer attached their client logs and a small snippet. They say it reliably happens on long generations (>20s).

maya: Customer Go snippet (redacted):
```go
ctx := context.Background()
c := redwood.NewClient(apiKey)
it, err := c.NewStreaming(ctx, opts)
for it.Next() {
  tok := it.Token()
  fmt.Print(tok)
}
if err := it.Err(); err != nil {
  log.Println("stream error:", err)
}
```

eli: Which http.Transport settings are they using? Any custom timeouts or proxies?

maya: Default http.Client, no proxy. They did set `ReadTimeout` on their net/http server but not on the client.

john: Can you reproduce with raw curl against the SSE endpoint? That will tell us if it's server-side SSE formatting vs SDK parsing.

maya: I tried curl from the customer logs (they included the exact curl) — curl stream stays open and delivers the final token every time. Only the Go SDK path drops the last chunk.

tilly: ops-bot, did we deploy anything touching streaming parsers around the timeframe they upgraded?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: inference-runtime deployed sha:abcd1234 at 2025-11-18T03:22:11Z. no streaming-parser changes in runtime; go-sdk bumped to v1.4.0 in the SDK repo.

eli: OK that points to the Go SDK. I'm going to try to reproduce locally with v1.4.0.

(10m later)

eli: Repro'd locally. Behavior: when the server sends a long token sequence and then the connection hiccups, the SDK reconnect logic tries to resume using Last-Event-ID but the iterator sometimes returns with `Next()` true then `Token()` empty for the last event, so the final newline-delimited `data:` chunk is dropped.

eli: Root cause: we switched to a buffered `bufio.Scanner` in 1.4.0 and relied on `Scan()` for `

` delimiter detection. Scanner has a max token size and also can split on CRLF in a way that collapses the blank line separator in some edge cases when there is backpressure. On reconnect we resume but we don't re-emit the last buffered partial chunk.

eli: Repro steps I used:
1) run a simple SSE server that yields a long generation (simulate tokens every 50ms for ~25s)
2) kill the TCP connection with `pkill -f` mid-stream
3) observe iterator returns and then a reconnect; sometimes final data missing

Code to simulate server (toy):
```go
// sends many small chunks then sleeps 
for i := 0; i < 1000; i++ {
  fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: token-%d\n\n", i)
  w.(http.Flusher).Flush()
  time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
}
```

eli: Quick debug patch I applied locally: stop using `bufio.Scanner` and use `ReadBytes('\n')`/manual buffer so we always preserve trailing partial chunk on reconnect and treat double newline correctly. Small pseudo-fix: read lines into a bytes.Buffer until we hit an empty line, then emit joined buffer.

eli: Patch applied to my local SDK build fixed the repro consistently. I also reproduced the customer binary with the patch — no missing final tokens and reconnect resumes correctly.

john: Can you open a PR with the fix and mark it high priority? Include tests that simulate fragmented SSE chunks and kill+resume scenarios.

eli: Will do. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/789 (draft) — includes a unit test that simulates network chunking and a reconnection.

maya: Customer confirmed that applying the patched binary resolved their issue. They were on a tight timeline and patched their vendor binary locally.

maya: Customer also mentioned a related symptom: sometimes they saw duplicate tokens immediately after reconnect. Is that covered?

eli: Duplicate tokens are expected if resume semantics overlap — we use Last-Event-ID resume which can replay the last event. We should dedupe on the client side using last-emitted-event-id to avoid duplicates. I'll add a small dedupe guard in the iterator to drop an identical immediate-repeat token on resume.

john: Good. Triage notes:
- Cause: go-sdk 1.4.0 buffering change introduced edge-case with bufio.Scanner and SSE chunking.
- Fix: switch to manual delimiting using ReadBytes('\n') and add dedupe on resume.
- Hotfix: cut release 1.4.1 with the patch and publish to customers.
- Backport: patch to 1.3.x branch if needed.

deploy-bot: staging release created: go-sdk v1.4.1-rc1.

tilly: I'll coordinate with SRE/Support to notify customers and update the support KB about the specific v1.4.0 issue. Add note to status page: affected clients using go-sdk v1.4.0 may see partial SSE streams on long generations; upgrade to v1.4.1 to fix.

maya: Assigned ticket to eng-runtime (eli) and devex (john) to track release and KB update. Customer follow-up: scheduled call tomorrow to validate upgrade.

john: Add a regression test in CI that simulates chunked SSE + reconnect; make it part of SDK pre-release gating.

eli: PR merged to main after tests. v1.4.1 published. Backport PR opened for 1.3.x.

maya: Customer confirmed on the call that after upgrading to v1.4.1 the streams are stable and the last token shows up. Closing ticket once we've pushed the KB. :tada:

tilly: KB update done: https://confluence.redwood/infr/streaming-sse-go-sdk-1.4.0-bug . Marking incident as resolved.

john: Nice catch. Leaving a note for runtime folks: streaming parsers are fragile with chunked delivery; try to avoid bufio.Scanner for protocol parsing unless token size limits are accounted for.

maya: Closing thread.
